title: LiteLLM v1.110.0rc3 fixes fallback overrides and WebSocket model aliases
points: A string fallback override such as `"fallbacks": "default"` no longer returns 500, and other invalid override values return 400.
Responses WebSocket requests keep the team's model alias, as HTTP `/v1/responses` does.
Hugging Face chat honors `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE`, and unmapped Fireworks AI models sized like `1p5b` bill at the up-to-4B rate.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.9 (LTS) adds Vertex labels and fixes Foundry /openai/v1
points: Set `litellm_settings.vertex_request_label_fields` to label Vertex calls with the caller's key, team, org and project, so Cloud Billing splits Vertex spend.
Azure deployments on Foundry project and resource `/openai/v1` URLs serve Responses and chat calls, and `api_version: none` sends no `api-version`.
Bedrock Converse reads `s3://` images, PDFs and videos as S3 sources, and OpenAI-style filters work on Bedrock knowledge base search.

title: LiteLLM v1.106.10 fixes repeated sign-in on Google MCP servers
points: Google MCP servers keep users signed in after the access token expires.
The proxy requests offline access from Google upstream OAuth providers, so each Google MCP connection gets a refresh token.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.8 (LTS) fixes Azure Decisions calls and an MCP sign-in loop
points: `azure/` deployments no longer return 400 on `/v1/decisions`.
MCP sign-in no longer loops to `Authentication incomplete` on servers that answer `mcp_all` with detailed scopes.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.7 (LTS) adds Gemini batches and Bedrock image search
points: `/v1/batches` runs Gemini batches with output download through `/v1/files`, and Bedrock knowledge bases accept image search with `query_image`.
Azure AI Foundry deployments support gpt-image edits, and Gemini image calls bill text, thinking and Vertex Priority tokens at the correct rates.
Responses-only fields such as `max_tool_calls` return 400 on providers bridged through chat completions unless you set `drop_params: true`.

title: LiteLLM v1.109.1 and v1.110.0rc2 reject Azure login fields in the body
points: Model and pass-through routes reject `tenant_id`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `azure_username`, `azure_password` and `azure_scope` in the request body.
Send these fields in `metadata`, or set `general_settings.allow_client_side_credentials: true` or `configurable_clientside_auth_params` to restore the old behavior.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.6 (LTS) fixes negative spend and Gemini image edit cost
points: Key, user and team spend no longer goes negative after a scheduled budget reset on multi-pod deployments.
Gemini image edits bill by tokens instead of a flat per-image price, and Zscaler AI Guard scans only the latest user message.
Model routes reject `tenant_id`, `client_id`, `client_secret` and Azure login fields in the body, so move them to `metadata` or set `allow_client_side_credentials`.

title: LiteLLM v1.106.9 forwards ChatGPT logins and rejects Azure body fields
points: Codex and Pi keep their own ChatGPT login through the gateway, and a client ChatGPT login takes precedence over a saved gateway login.
Model routes reject `tenant_id`, `client_id`, `client_secret` and Azure login fields in the body, so move them to `metadata` or set `allow_client_side_credentials`.

title: LiteLLM v1.107.0rc4 adds a CLI command to link GitHub Copilot accounts
points: `lite credentials connect` links a per-user GitHub Copilot credential from the terminal, so developers without Admin UI access can use Copilot.
The Docker images ship newer `aiohttp`, `ddtrace`, `pypdf` and other locked dependencies.

title: LiteLLM v1.107.0rc3 fixes GitHub Copilot per-user connect and adds GHE.com
points: GitHub Copilot per-user credentials work on GHE.com tenants with the optional `github_copilot_host` field.
Per-user Copilot connect no longer fails with `no Copilot access found` when `GITHUB_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` is set.

title: LiteLLM v1.110.0rc1 adds the Agent Skills Hub and a Rust-only router
points: The router always runs on the Rust core, and a router config that the Rust core declines now stops the proxy at startup.
Spend goes through the `LiteLLM_SpendLogDelivery` ledger by default, and `general_settings.use_spend_logs_ledger: false` restores the previous spend queues.
The Agent Skills Hub adds skill upload and import, version history and an admin review queue for member submissions.
Streamed `/v1/responses` no longer ends with `[DONE]`, and raw response ids that the proxy did not issue are rejected by default.

title: LiteLLM v1.106.8 fixes transcription cost for some FLAC files
points: Transcription cost is correct for some FLAC files that could push a key over its budget.
Per-second transcriptions bill the `usage.seconds` that the provider reports, so spend matches the provider invoice and unmeasured files no longer log $0.

title: LiteLLM v1.104.9 and v1.103.11 speed up request lookups in the Logs view
points: After migrations, the proxy builds the spend log indexes that some installs lack, so request lookups in the Logs view stay fast on large tables.
On v1.103.11, replicas that boot together against one database start up more reliably while a peer runs or recovers migrations.

title: LiteLLM v1.109.0 adds 11 providers, Codex tool search and daily limits
points: LiteLLM adds 11 providers, including ai&, StreamLake, OpenInfer and BigModel, among 311 new model catalog entries.
Codex discovers MCP tools through tool search, and deployments accept `rpd` and `tpd` daily limits.
Streams that stall, abort or end without a finish reason now fail visibly, so retries, cooldowns and fallbacks apply to them.
Claude models missing from the cost map now default to `max_tokens: 128000`, and `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_CHAT_MAX_TOKENS=4096` keeps the old value.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.5 (LTS) fixes workload identity on OpenAI routes and transcription cost
points: Keyless workload identity OpenAI deployments no longer answer 401 on image edits, audio, files, batches and the other routes beyond chat.
Transcription cost is correct for some FLAC files that could push a key over its budget.
`ollama_chat/` streams give each parallel tool call its own index, and `/v1/messages` honors a deployment's `additional_drop_params`.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.4 (LTS) fixes Bedrock pass-through guardrails and video polls
points: The `/bedrock` pass-through routes enforce the model's `guardrailConfig`, and it replaces any guardrail the caller sends.
Video status and content polls keep their model, so per-model keys work and each poll reaches the account that created the video.
A base SDK install no longer fails with `No module named 'mcp'` when `completion()`, `responses()` or `messages` get a tool.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.3 (LTS) fixes Bedrock api_base and large MCP tool results
points: Bedrock deployments with `api_base: ""` serve requests again, and no longer return 500 or 400.
MCP tool results over 1 MiB no longer fail with `SSE stream ended without a response`, and model-level `post_call` guardrails check each response once.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.2 (LTS) fixes Bedrock service tiers and Claude PDF input
points: Bedrock Converse honors the `reserved`, `auto` and `standard_only` service tiers and returns 400 for a tier that it does not support.
Base64 PDFs that you send to Claude as `image_url` work, and `openai/` deployments with an empty `api_key` no longer send `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY`.
Groups that accept unmatched tags keep the request after affinity or cooldown filters.

title: LiteLLM v1.108.1 (LTS) fixes Bedrock guardrail billing and router cooldowns
points: A string fallback target such as `default_fallbacks: gpt-3.5` stops the proxy at startup, so write it as a list, `default_fallbacks: ["gpt-3.5"]`.
Spend and budgets include native Bedrock guardrail traces and the Gemini audio rates for flex, priority and batch.
The router keeps the only deployment of a group warm under `allowed_fails`, and evicted SDK clients close their aiohttp sessions.

title: LiteLLM v1.106.7 supports custom video providers on /v1/videos
points: `/v1/videos` serves providers that `custom_provider_map` registers.
The proxy and its Helm charts no longer package the Lens beta, so remove `lensWorker.enabled` from your Helm values before you upgrade.
